name: Winterhoof Cleansing Totem
summary: At Winterhoof Water Well, poisoned water threatens the herds and tribes of Mulgore. Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem to cleanse the well.

sections.title: Purifying the Spring
sections.body:
Mull Thunderhorn crafts the Winterhoof Cleansing Totem in Bloodhoof Village. Venture Company goblins have tainted Mulgore's underground water through their operations. He charms the carved wood to wash away those foreign poisons.

The totem must be carried past hostile goblin guards to Winterhoof Water Well. There, a focused ritual disperses the contamination. Pure drinking water returns for the plains' wandering herds and native tribes.

faq.q: What is the Winterhoof Cleansing Totem used for?
faq.answer: You carry the totem to Winterhoof Water Well, southeast of Bloodhoof Village, and perform a ritual to scour contamination from the aquifer.
Mull Thunderhorn, a respected tauren of Bloodhoof Village, carves and prepares the totem to undo the harm to Winterhoof Water Well.

faq.q: Why was the Winterhoof Water Well polluted?
faq.answer: The Venture Company sets up an encampment around the spring. Runoff, waste and chemical sludge from its logging and mining machinery pollute the natural watering hole.

faq.q: What happens once the cleansing ritual is complete?
faq.answer: After the ritual, the murky water is clean and wholesome again. Local wildlife and migrating tauren herds can safely drink from the well.

angles.text: For tauren, the desecration of fresh water wounds their bond with the Earth Mother. The totem's rite helps defend their homeland.
As a shaman, you call on the harmony of earth and water to cast out artificial corruption. The rite follows shamanic principles.
